title.en: Rescuers search for survivors of powerful Indonesia earthquake
title.zh: 救援人员搜寻印度尼西亚强震幸存者

summary.en: A powerful earthquake in Indonesia has destroyed hundreds of buildings and killed 47 people, with officials conducting a rapid assessment and rescuers searching for survivors.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚发生强烈地震，摧毁了数百座建筑物，造成47人死亡。目前，官员们正在进行快速评估，救援人员正在搜寻幸存者。

body.en:
Rescue teams in Indonesia have been searching for survivors of Saturday's major earthquake which left at least 47 people dead.

The magnitude 7.7 quake struck the island of Flores shortly before 05:00 (22:00 GMT on Friday) and had a depth of 15km, Indonesia's meteorology and geophysics agency stated.

Preliminary reports indicated more than 900 homes and hundreds of other buildings were damaged severely by the quake and 341 aftershocks, the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) agency said.

However, the full scale of the disaster is still unclear, and news of a second earthquake of magnitude 6.9 at the other end of Indonesia served as a reminder of why this region is called the ring of fire.

Tremors from Saturday's powerful earthquake were reportedly felt by residents as far west as Bima Regency and City, the BNPB said, but the Manggarai province is among the most affected.

Preliminary data shows that 24 fatalities had been recorded there, meanwhile 17 deaths were recorded in East Manggarai province, three in Sikka province, and at least one in each of the Ngada, Ende and West Manggarai provinces.

The BNPB said more than 5,000 people remained in evacuation shelters and aid 10,500 aid packages have been sent to affected areas.

"Meeting basic needs and providing logistics for evacuees has become one of the top priorities of the emergency response," the BNPB said.

It will take time to assess the full extent of the destruction in the region, which is remote and mountainous.

However, early reports indicate more than 150 houses had been severely damaged, as well as dozens of educational institutions, a number of healthcare facilities, places of worship, offices, and several other public facilities.

Video taken at the port in Maumere - the largest town in Flores - showed large chunks of concrete breaking off the terminal building onto passengers waiting to board an inter-island ferry. Some were thrown into the sea when the gangway to a ship collapsed.

Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena, governor of East Nusa Tenggara province, told a news conference that they were killed in their sleep by collapsing rubble.

Others, like Arnold Welianto, who lives in Talibura, a village near the coastline in Sikka, East Nusa Tenggara, were shaken out of their beds.

He also told the BBC that many people had already fled into the hills because the sea had also receded.

While a tsunami warning was initially issued - leading some 2,000 people to self-evacuate - it was lifted around three hours after the initial jolt, when no significant sea level rise was detected.

Landslides, however, did block access to some villages but the experienced rescue teams worked tirelessly through the day to free those trapped under the rubble.

body.zh: 印度尼西亚的救援队一直在寻找星期六大地震的幸存者，这场地震造成至少 47 人死亡。 印度尼西亚气象和地球物理机构表示，在 05:00（格林威治标准时间周五 22:00）前不久，弗洛勒斯岛发生了 7.7 级地震，震源深度为 15 公里。 初步报告显示，数百座建筑物在地震和随后发生的数十次余震中严重受损。 然而，灾难的全面规模仍不清楚，印度尼西亚另一端发生第二次6.9级地震的消息提醒人们为什么他们称该地区为火环。 国家灾害管理局（BNPB）表示，据报道，远至西边的比马县和市的居民都感受到了周六强烈地震带来的震动，但芒加莱省是受影响最严重的省份之一。 初步数据显示，该地区已造成 24 人死亡，同时东芒加莱省有 17 人死亡，锡卡省有 3 人死亡，恩加达省、恩德省和西芒加莱省各至少有 1 人死亡。 BNPB 表示，目前已有 10,500 个包裹抵达基地，援助物资正在运往受影响地区。 该地区地处偏远，多山，需要时间来评估其破坏的全面程度。 然而，早期报告显示，150 多所房屋以及数十个教育机构、一些医疗设施、礼拜场所、办公室和其他一些公共设施遭到严重损坏。 在弗洛勒斯最大城镇毛梅雷的港口拍摄的视频显示，航站楼上有大块混凝土脱落，砸在等待登上岛际渡轮的乘客身上。当一艘船的舷梯倒塌时，一些人被扔进海里。 东努沙登加拉省省长伊曼纽尔·梅尔基亚德斯·拉卡·莱纳在新闻发布会上说，他们在睡梦中被倒塌的瓦砾炸死。 其他人，比如住在东努沙登加拉省锡卡海岸线附近塔利布拉村的阿诺德·韦利安托(Arnold Welianto)，都被从床上摇了起来。 他还告诉BBC，由于海水也退去了，许多人已经逃进山里。 虽然最初发布了海啸警报，导致约 2,000 人自行疏散，但在最初的震动大约三个小时后解除，当时没有检测到海平面明显上升。 然而，山体滑坡确实封锁了通往一些村庄的道路，但经验丰富的救援队全天不知疲倦地工作，以解救被困在废墟下的人们。 在如腾，医院外还搭建了临时医疗帐篷，用于救治地震灾民。 BNPB 持续建议人们保持冷静，远离沿海地区……

body.en: The Guardian travelled 100 miles along the EU’s longest river, where some residents are struggling to secure drinking water For centuries, the rock was seen as a warning. When it began to emerge from the Danube, beneath Gellért Hill in Budapest, it meant the river had fallen so low that floating mills could no longer operate, crops were probably failing, and hunger would almost certainly follow. That is why, in the Hungarian capital, where over time the boulder became little more than a legend, it was named Ínség-szikla – the Rock of Starvation. Today, amid record-low water levels on the Danube, the rock has not only emerged from the water, but surfaced almost in its entirety, along with the sandy riverbed on which it rests, astonishing geologists and government scientists sent to examine it. And, much as the rock was said to warn, Hungary is now facing an unprecedented energy crisis that has forced the country to shut down all but one of its Danube-cooled nuclear reactors for the first time in 44 years. title.en: Hawaii braces for potential first direct hit by a hurricane in 34 years
title.zh: 夏威夷为34年来首次飓风直接袭击做准备

summary.en: Hawaii is preparing for Hurricane Lala, which could be the first direct hit in 34 years, with a worst-case scenario predicting up to 25 inches (63cm) of rain on Big Island.
summary.zh: 夏威夷正为飓风拉拉可能带来的34年来首次直接袭击做准备，最坏情况下，大岛可能降下多达25英寸（63厘米）的雨量。

body.en:
Hawaii is bracing for what could be its first direct hit from a hurricane since 1992, as category one storm Lala churns off its coast.

With wind speeds as high as 80mph (130km/h), Lala gained hurricane strength on Saturday. In a worst-case scenario, it could dump up to 25in (63cm) of rain on Big Island and produce a 3ft storm surge.

A hurricane warning is in effect for Big Island, while Maui County, Oahu, Kauai and Niihau are under tropical storm warnings. Officials have told residents to prepare for "life-threatening" conditions, including floods and mudslides.

The storm is expected to either make landfall or pass close to the southern tip of Big Island on Saturday, before continuing west.

In an update at 17:00 local time (03:00 GMT), the National Hurricane Center said Lala's eye wall was "brushing the southern portion of the Big Island".

"Damaging winds a heavy rain will persist across the Big Island throughout tonight and spread westwards across the smaller islands on Sunday," it said.

The last time a hurricane made landfall on Hawaii's Big Island was 155 years ago, according to the Associated Press news agency.

Over the weekend, Lala will continue moving westwards, and may weaken into a tropical storm, with the centre passing just below Hawaii's other islands.

Hawaii Governor Josh Green warned residents to brace for "an incredible amount of water".

"Damaging winds, heavy rain, flash flooding and dangerous surf are possible across the state through the weekend," he posted on X.

At Ellison Onizuka Kona International - Big Island's largest airport - 40% of flights were grounded, according to flightaware.com. Some 80% of flights were called off at its other main airport, Hilo International.

The more dire forecasts from the National Weather Service (NWS) have been issued for areas within Big Island's south-east.

"Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues," the NWS said, adding that rivers and tributaries "may rapidly overflow their banks in multiple places".

Nearly 37,000 customers had lost electricity on Hawaii as of Saturday afternoon, according to the website poweroutage.us.

Meteorologist Jennifer Myers, who lives in Hilo, eastern Big Island, said landslides had already cut off some roads, while power lines had been ripped down by falling trees.

"I'm looking at the river right now, and it's really, really high," she told the BBC about the view from her apartment of the Wailuku River as it meets Hilo Bay.

"The bay that's usually blue is like blood red right now because of all the sediment and river water in it."

Local message boards on Facebook show residents filling bags with sand to protect their homes and inquiring whether stores remained open in the early hours on Saturday.

title.en: BBC seeks to subpoena family members in Panorama lawsuit
title.zh: 英国广播公司寻求传唤特朗普家人参与《广角镜》诉讼

summary.en: The BBC's legal team is attempting to subpoena former President Trump's family members, asserting they possess "personal knowledge" regarding his intentions during the speech delivered outside the US Capitol on January 6, 2021.
summary.zh: 英国广播公司的律师们正试图传唤前总统特朗普的家人，声称他们对特朗普在2021年1月6日美国国会大厦外发表的演讲意图“有个人了解”。

body.en:
The BBC has sought to subpoena members of Donald Trump's family for documents and testimony in the US president's $10bn (£7.4bn) defamation lawsuit against the broadcaster.

Court filings show that representatives for the BBC's legal team attempted in May to serve subpoenas to the president's son Donald Trump Jr, his daughter Ivanka Trump and son-in-law Jared Kushner.

The president is suing the BBC over an episode of Panorama that edited together two different sections of a speech he gave before the 2021 Capitol riots.

The BBC has previously apologised for the edit, but denied it was grounds for defamation.

In a statement to the BBC, a spokesman for Trump's legal team said the BBC had "intentionally defamed" the president, and with its subpoena request was now "seeking to harass him, his family, and supporters by abusing the deposition process".

"The BBC is simply trying to distract away from their own obvious liability," the statement said.

The BBC's lawyers argue in the latest filing that Trump's family members had "personal knowledge" of his intentions in delivering the speech, making their testimony and documents relevant to the president's defamation claim.

Drawing on evidence previously gathered by a US congressional committee, the filing says Donald Trump Jr and Ivanka Trump were present when their father revised and delivered his speech, adding that Jared Kushner drafted a proposed statement for him that would have condemned the use of violence.

The filing asks the court to allow the subpoenas to be served by email and certified mail, saying attempts to serve them by hand were unsuccessful.

A subpoena is an order for someone to answer questions under oath or provide evidence. Failure to comply results in a penalty.

According to court filings, in one instance, a representative for the BBC's legal team tried to deliver a subpoena for Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner at their home in Florida, but was refused entry at a police checkpoint and was later told by the Secret Service that the agency could not accept the subpoenas.

Similarly, according to the filing, a representative tried to serve a subpoena for Donald Trump Jr at Trump Tower in New York but was told by the concierge that the person who normally took such documents may have been at lunch.

During another attempt two days later, the representative was told the "legal department" was not in that day, according to the filing.

Last December, Trump sued the BBC and subsidiaries BBC Studios Productions and BBC Studios Distribution over the 2024 Panorama episode.

Trump's lawsuit - filed in Florida - accuses the BBC of "intentionally, maliciously and deceptively doctoring" the speech he gave outside the Capitol on 6 January 2021.

body.zh: BBC 已寻求传唤唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 的家人，以获取美国总统针对该广播公司提起的 100 亿美元（74 亿英镑）诽谤诉讼中的文件和证词。 法庭文件显示，BBC 法律团队的代表于 5 月试图向总统的儿子小唐纳德·特朗普、女儿伊万卡·特朗普和女婿贾里德·库什纳发出传票。 总统正在起诉 BBC，因为该节目将他在 2021 年国会大厦骚乱之前发表的演讲的两个不同部分剪辑在一起。 BBC 此前已就编辑内容道歉，但否认这是诽谤的理由。 特朗普法律团队的发言人在给英国广播公司的一份声明中表示，英国广播公司“故意诽谤”总统，其传票请求现在“试图通过滥用证词程序来骚扰他、他的家人和支持者”。 声明称：“BBC 只是想转移人们对自己明显责任的注意力。” BBC 的律师在最新的文件中辩称，特朗普的家人“个人了解”他发表演讲的意图，他们的证词和文件与总统的诽谤指控相关。 该文件根据美国国会委员会之前收集的证据，称小唐纳德·特朗普和伊万卡·特朗普在父亲修改并发表演讲时在场，并补充说贾里德·库什纳为他起草了一份谴责使用暴力的拟议声明。 该文件要求法院允许通过电子邮件和挂号信送达传票，并称手工送达传票的尝试未成功。 传票是要求某人宣誓回答问题或提供证据的命令。不遵守规定将受到处罚。 根据法庭文件，有一次，BBC 法律团队的一名代表试图在伊万卡·特朗普和贾里德·库什纳位于佛罗里达州的家中向伊万卡·特朗普和贾里德·库什纳发出传票，但在警察检查站被拒绝进入，后来特勤局告知该机构不能接受传票。 同样，根据文件，一名代表试图在纽约特朗普大厦向小唐纳德·特朗普发出传票，但礼宾部告诉，通常拿走此类文件的人可能正在吃午饭。 文件显示，在两天后的另一次尝试中，该代表被告知“法律部门”当天不在。 我们已联系特朗普的法律团队征求意见。 BBC 新闻办公室拒绝置评。 去年 12 月，特朗普就 2024 年全景剧集起诉 BBC 及其子公司 BBC Studios Productions 和 BBC Studios Distribution。 特朗普在佛罗里达州提起的诉讼指控英国广播公司“故意、恶意和欺骗性地篡改”他的演讲。

reflection.en: In complex situations, understanding the full truth often requires hearing from multiple perspectives and examining all available information. This legal effort to gather testimony from those with personal knowledge reflects the wisdom that a case isn't fully understood until all sides have been heard and scrutinized. reflection.zh: 在复杂的情况下，要了解全部真相，往往需要听取多方观点并审视所有可用信息。这项旨在从知情者那里收集证词的法律努力，反映了一种智慧，即在各方都被听取和审查之前，案件无法被完全理解。雅伟鼓励我们在下结论之前寻求彻底的理解。

body.en:
At least 11 people have been killed in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon, the Lebanese health ministry said, some of the deadliest raids since deals in June eased hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah.

The Israeli military said it struck Hezbollah infrastructure overnight in what it describes as a security zone in southern Lebanon in response to actions against its soldiers there.

Iran-backed Hezbollah said in a statement that the attacks would be "met with what they deserve".

The framework leaves Israeli troops inside occupied southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed and the Lebanese army takes control, terms the group has rejected as surrender.

Lebanon's official National News Agency said seven people were killed when Israeli warplanes struck a house in the southern village of Ansar, while four others were killed in a strike on the village of Deir El Zahrani.

NNA also reported other airstrikes across southern Lebanon, including on a strategic area north of the Litani River known as Ali al-Taher hill. One, targeting a valley next to Ansar, was the deepest strike into Lebanon in two months.

The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in a statement on X, accused Hezbollah of violating the ceasefire and attacking Israeli soldiers leading to three injuries.

"The IDF (Israel Defense Forces) responded by striking the Hezbollah terror headquarters which ordered the attack," the statement said. "Only later did the IDF learn that Hezbollah deliberately put civilians in that military compound."

The Israeli military said in a statement it killed Ali Samir Al-Haj Hassan, a commander in Hezbollah's elite Radwan Force unit and others when it struck "a central headquarters of the Radwan Force unit", in Ansar.

"At the time of the strike, Hassan’s family was also present with him inside the military headquarters and, according to the claim, was harmed in the strike," the statement added, emphasising that the family was not the target of the strike.

title.en: Australian state to launch gun buyback after Bondi Beach attack
title.zh: 澳大利亚一州将在邦迪海滩袭击后启动枪支回购计划

summary.en: New South Wales, Australia, is implementing a gun buyback scheme. This initiative follows a recent attack in Bondi Beach and aims to reduce the number of firearms in circulation by offering cash to gun owners who surrender their weapons.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚新南威尔士州将在邦迪海滩袭击事件后启动一项枪支回购计划。该计划将向枪支拥有者提供现金，以收缴他们的枪支，旨在减少流通中的枪支数量。

body.en:
Australia's most populous state will launch a gun buyback scheme later this year, becoming the first to offer cash in exchange for firearms following the Bondi Beach terror attack.

Gun owners in New South Wales (NSW) will be offered up to AUS$1,000 (£523) to hand over eligible handguns, shotguns and rifles from 2 November.

Australian authorities had pledged sweeping firearm law reforms after 15 people were shot dead at a Jewish festival on Sydney's Bondi Beach, which is located in NSW, last December.

The state's Premier Chris Minns said on Saturday: "We want those guns handed in, compensated for and safely destroyed."

Gun ownership reforms already introduced by the state mean individuals can only own four firearms - although some people, such as farmers and sports shooters, can own a maximum of 10.

The scheme will be offered to those who have more weapons than permitted by the new rules, or who are no longer covered by a licence - with terms having been reduced from five years to two.

The scheme will be implemented in two phases. The first - from the start of November - covers types of handguns, shotguns and rifles.

Those handing over a revolver, for example, will be paid AUS$1,000, while an air rifle will fetch AUS$450.

The second phase will begin early next year and cover "higher-value firearms" valued above AUS$3,000, capped at AUS$10,000.

The National Gun BuyBack Scheme is being jointly funded by New South Wales and the federal government.

Businesses will be able to receive up to AUS$25,000 in support to help them adjust to the reforms, with help also offered to gun-dealers.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said: "We must do everything we can to make sure the antisemitic terrorist attack in Bondi doesn't happen again.

On 14 December last year, 15 people including a 10-year-old girl and a Holocaust survivor were killed as Hanukkah celebrations took place along Australia's famed beachfront.

Australian authorities had initially planned a nationwide gun buyback, though plans have been delayed over funding and questions about how it would be implemented.
body.zh: 澳大利亚人口最多的州将于今年晚些时候推出枪支回购计划，成为邦迪海滩恐怖袭击后第一个提供现金换取枪支的州。 从 11 月 2 日起，新南威尔士州 (NSW) 的枪支拥有者将获得高达 1,000 澳元（523 英镑）的补贴，以交出符合条件的手枪、霰弹枪和步枪。 去年 12 月，在新南威尔士州悉尼邦迪海滩的犹太节日上有 15 人被枪杀后，澳大利亚当局承诺对枪支法进行全面改革。 该州州长克里斯·明斯(Chris Minns)周六表示：“我们希望这些枪支被上交、赔偿并安全销毁。” 国家已经推行的枪支所有权改革意味着个人只能拥有四支枪支——尽管有些人，例如农民和体育射击运动员，最多可以拥有 10 支枪支。 该计划将提供给那些拥有比新规则允许的武器数量更多的人，或者不再受许可证保护的人——期限从五年减少到两年。 该计划将分两个阶段实施。第一个 - 从 11 月初开始 - 涵盖手枪、霰弹枪和步枪的类型。 例如，交出一把左轮手枪的人将获得 1,000 澳元的报酬，而交出一把气步枪的人将获得 450 澳元的报酬。 第二阶段将于明年初开始，涵盖价值 3,000 澳元以上的“高价值枪支”，上限为 10,000 澳元。 国家枪支回购计划由新南威尔士州和联邦政府共同资助。 企业将能够获得高达 25,000 澳元的支持，以帮助他们适应改革，枪支经销商也可以获得帮助。 总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞表示：“我们必须尽一切努力确保邦迪反犹太主义恐怖袭击不再发生。 去年12月14日，在澳大利亚最著名的海滩附近举行光明节庆祝活动时，包括一名10岁女孩和一名大屠杀幸存者在内的15人被杀。 澳大利亚当局最初计划在全国范围内回购枪支，但该计划因资金和实施方式而被推迟。

title.zh: 印度尼西亚地震造成数十人死亡，救援人员绝望搜寻幸存者

summary.en: Rescue teams are urgently working to reach the region closest to the epicenter of an Indonesian earthquake, where landslides have blocked roads and dozens of people have been killed.
summary.zh: 救援队正紧急赶往印度尼西亚地震震中附近地区，那里山体滑坡阻断了道路，已有数十人遇难。

body.en:
Rescuers have combed through debris for survivors after a powerful earthquake struck off Indonesia's eastern Flores island , killing 48 people and injuring dozens, according to disaster officials.

The national disaster management agency (BNPB) raised the death toll from 40 late on Saturday, and rescue official Fathur Rahman said 50 people were injured in the 7.7-magnitude quake.

Suharyanto, who leads the BNPB, said earlier that people were trapped in several buildings.

"These will be the initial targets of the disaster response teams," said Suharyanto, who like many Indonesians uses one name.

Nearly 160 houses, dozens of educational and health facilities and other public buildings were damaged when the earthquake struck the popular tourist island in Indonesia's east, the BNPB reported.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said preparations were underway to bring aid to some 2,000 people in temporary shelters.

The government sent 50,000 aid packages weighing a total of 275 tonnes to the area, and European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen offered help from the bloc's Copernicus Earth observation satellites.

"Europe stands ready to deploy Copernicus, our eyes in the sky, to support search and rescue efforts. Indonesia, we stand with you," she wrote on X.

"I have never felt an earthquake this big," Yulian Juita Ekalia, who lives in Ruteng city more than 100 kilometres west of the epicentre, told AFP by telephone hours after the tremor.

"It felt like we were on a trampoline; it was really scary," said the 37-year-old university lecturer, who was jolted awake at around 5.30am local time on Saturday.

"As I rushed to get outside, everything in the house fell down: the television, my son's trophies, the dish racks, suitcases on top of the wardrobes. When I got outside, my son and neighbours were already there, screaming in fear."

Rescue official Fathur told AFP the focus was on locating victims who may be buried under rubble, but rescue efforts have been complicated by landslides cutting off roads.

Residents in Nagekeo, an area close to the epicentre, raced for higher ground as the sea retreated early Saturday — a possible sign of an approaching tsunami , AFP journalists witnessed.

While a tsunami warning was lifted, authorities urged people not to return to damaged buildings for fear that aftershocks may bring them down.

Hundreds remained outside hours later as dozens of aftershocks shook the island, the strongest measured at a magnitude of 6.1.

reflection.en: In the wake of such devastating loss and desperate searches, our hearts ache for those affected by the earthquake. Revelation 21:4 reminds us of Yahweh's promise to one day wipe away every tear, where death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more. This hope offers solace even as we grieve with those who suffer today.
reflection.zh: 在这场毁灭性的灾难和绝望的搜救之后，我们的心为所有受地震影响的人而痛。启示录21:4提醒我们雅伟的应许，有一天祂将擦去所有的眼泪，不再有死亡、悲哀、哭号和疼痛。这个盼望在今天我们与受苦者一同悲伤时，提供了安慰。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: Qatar denies capturing three Iranian pilots after downing fighter jets
title.zh: 卡塔尔否认击落战斗机后俘虏三名伊朗飞行员

summary.en: Qatar has denied Iran's claims that it has held three Iranian pilots since Qatar downed two fighter jets at the start of the US-Iran war.
summary.zh: 卡塔尔否认了伊朗的指控，即在美伊战争爆发之初卡塔尔击落两架战斗机后，卡塔尔一直扣押着三名伊朗飞行员。

body.en:
Iran has called for the release of three pilots it said were captured by Qatar after two of its fighter jets were hit by air defences during a military operation at the start of the US-Iran war.

In a letter to the head of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), Iran's Brig Gen Mohammad Bagherzadeh said the pilots - Javad Salehi, Abdul Majid Dashtian and Imran Behroshian - had been held captive for six months.

He said the body of a fourth pilot, Majid Kazemi, had been returned after he was killed in the same operation on 2 March 2026 - the third day of the war.

Qatar "categorically denied" Iran's claims and said it was "surprised by these misleading statements".

Gen Bagherzadeh said the three pilots had been captured by Qatar after they ejected from their jets during a combat mission targeting a Qatari military base.

In the letter to ICRC chief Mirjana Spoljaric, published by Iranian media, he accused Qatar of violating "the inalienable rights of these prisoners, contrary to all international laws and regulations".

The letter also claimed the three pilots had not been allowed to meet or contact their families.

Qatar's foreign affairs spokesperson Majed Mohammed Al Ansari said contact had been made with the pilots "after they violated Qatari airspace", but that it had not received a response.

"The necessary measures were taken to defend our territory in accordance with international law," he added in a statement on X.

Al Ansari said Qatar's search and rescue teams "carried out their duties to the fullest extent in searching for the pilots' remains".

He said Qatar contacted Iran to "co-ordinate the handover of the remains of one of the pilots that were recovered" and that Tehran had yet to respond to an invitation to review details of the search and rescue operation.
body.zh: 伊朗呼吁释放三名伊朗飞行员，据称是在美伊战争开始时的一次军事行动中两架战斗机被防空系统击中后被卡塔尔俘虏的。 伊朗准将穆罕默德·巴格尔扎德在致红十字国际委员会主席的一封信中表示，这三名飞行员——贾瓦德·萨利希、阿卜杜勒·马吉德·达什蒂安和伊姆兰·贝罗希安——已被关押了六个月。 他说，第四名飞行员马吉德·卡泽米 (Majid Kazemi) 的尸体于 2026 年 3 月 2 日（即战争的第三天）在同一行动中丧生后被归还。 卡塔尔“断然否认”伊朗的说法，并表示“对这些误导性言论感到惊讶”。 巴格扎德将军表示，这三名飞行员在卡塔尔军事基地执行战斗任务时从飞机上弹射，随后被卡塔尔抓获。 在伊朗媒体发表的致红十字国际委员会主席米里亚娜·斯波尔贾里奇的信中，他指责卡塔尔侵犯了“这些囚犯不可剥夺的权利，违反了所有国际法律和法规”。 信中还声称，三名飞行员不被允许会见或联系他们的家人。 卡塔尔外交事务发言人马吉德·穆罕默德·安萨里表示，“在飞行员侵犯卡塔尔领空后”与他们进行了联系，但没有收到回应。 “我们根据国际法采取了必要措施来保卫我们的领土，”他在 X 的一份声明中补充道。 安萨里表示，卡塔尔搜救队“在搜寻飞行员遗体方面尽了最大努力”。 他说，卡塔尔已联系伊朗，“协调已找到的一名飞行员遗体的移交”，而德黑兰尚未回应审查搜救行动细节的邀请。

reflection.en: In times of international tension, conflicting claims and denials can obscure the truth and hinder efforts toward peace. Yahweh's word reminds us that speaking truthfully to one another is foundational for healthy relationships, whether between individuals or nations. When honesty is absent, trust erodes, making reconciliation difficult.
reflection.zh: 在国际局势紧张之时，相互矛盾的声明和否认会掩盖真相，阻碍和平努力。雅伟的话语提醒我们，彼此说实话是建立健康关系的基础，无论是个人之间还是国家之间。当缺乏诚实时，信任就会受到侵蚀，使和解变得困难。

verse.textEn: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to your neighbor.
verse.textZh: 所以你们要弃绝谎言，各人与邻舍说实话。

title.en: Fujisawa is in his 70s and was jailed 15 times for shoplifting. He was desperate to go back
title.zh: 70多岁的藤泽因盗窃入狱15次，他渴望再次回到监狱

summary.en: As living costs rise, a growing number of elderly people in Japan are resorting to theft. For some, prison is not a deterrent, it’s the goal.
summary.zh: 随着生活成本的上涨，日本越来越多的老年人开始盗窃。对一些人来说，监狱不是威慑，而是他们的目标。

body.en:
Watch Dateline’s latest episode, Japan’s Shoplifting Pensioners, on 18 August at 9.30pm AEST on SBS or SBS On Demand.

When Fujisawa walked out of prison for the fifteenth time, he had nowhere to go. No home, and no family waiting for him. After spending a total of 35 years behind bars for repeated shoplifting, remaining free meant uncertainty.

Fujisawa had been stealing tiny items of little use to him—lipstick, food, whatever he could grab quickly. Despite severe sentencing for repeat offenders in Japan, prison was never much of a deterrent. It meant returning to a community he was comfortable in.

"Once you’re in, you’re among friends, people who will accept who you are, whatever your background," he says.

Now in his seventies, Fujisawa has spent much of his adult life moving between prison and the outside world.

"I kept going in and out of prison," he says. I was only out in society for one or two years at a time."

While Fujisawa's story is extreme, he is part of a much broader problem in Japan.

Japan has one of the world's oldest populations, with more than a quarter of its citizens aged 65 or older. Its offenders are ageing too.

The proportion of elderly offenders has climbed despite overall crime rates falling dramatically. With people over 60 making up of more than a quarter of arrests in some parts of the country, many are accused of petty theft.

Volunteer probation officer Chiba has observed this shift. He says 20 to 30 per cent of his parolees are elderly.

"Being isolated and the rising cost of living, some old people don't receive enough pension. They run short on money, so they repeat crimes."

According to government data, around half of elderly people caught shoplifting live by themselves, with four in 10 saying they have no family or rarely speak to them.

The number of Japanese seniors living alone has dramatically increased over recent decades, leaving many to face old age with little financial or social support.

Elderly offenders also have some of Japan's highest rates of reoffending. Nearly one in five prisoners over 60 returns to prison within two years of being released.

Last year, the government amended the Penal Code, abolishing mandatory prison labour and introducing rehabilitation programs to give prisoners skills to help them cope with life on the outside.

But former prisoners coming back to the outside still face social stigma. Many struggle to find work and secure housing.

"Historically in Japan, our attitudes towards former prisoners and how we treat them has not been good," Chiba says .

title.en: 'It was like fan fiction': The strange story behind Fiji's origin myth
title.zh: 斐济与以色列深厚渊源背后的惊人故事

summary.en: Fiji's unexpected and strong relationship with Israel is rooted in a unique national origin story that has influenced both the island nation's local faith practices and its international diplomatic approach.
summary.zh: 斐济与以色列之间出人意料的紧密关系，植根于一个独特的国家起源故事，这个故事影响了斐济的乡村信仰实践及其国际外交政策。

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

Long ago, the story goes, a great double-hulled canoe called the Kaunitoni came from the west, carrying the first ancestral chiefs of the iTaukei (indigenous Fijians). At its head, in one version of the tradition, stood their leader, Lutunasobasoba.

The voyagers had come a seemingly impossible distance: from Thebes in ancient Egypt — earlier still, some say, from a place farther west, via Israel — down the Nile to Lake Tanganyika, across the Indian Ocean, and finally to Vuda, on the western coast of Viti Levu, Fiji's largest island.

In some tellings, it carried the written record of the people's laws and genealogies — lost, like the canoe's other cargo, somewhere in the churning sea.

For most of the past century, this has been one of the best-known versions of Fiji's national origin story. The mission schools taught it; so did the primary schools. Radio carried it further still, until it became part of the way generations of Fijians understood their ancestry.

Only, much of it was invented in the 1890s — set down for the first time in a newspaper.

The colonial government's Fijian-language paper, Na Mata, ran a competition at the time, inviting readers across the archipelago to send in the definitive account of where the Fijian people had come from, with the best to be printed.

The winning entry ran over 17 instalments, centring on a forgotten tribe. Within a few decades it had acquired the weight of history.

Behind the claimed migration sits a larger conviction, still widely held in some iTaukei communities and church groups: that Fijians descend from a Lost Tribe of Israel — one of 10 the Hebrew Bible describes as carried into exile and never heard from again.

The belief has no support in mainstream science or archaeology. Yet it has helped foster a distinctive affinity with Israel.

The particulars shift from place to place. On Mana Island, in the Yasawa group off western Viti Levu, the Ark of the Covenant — the gold-covered chest that, in the Book of Exodus, held the Ten Commandments — is said to lie buried.

In a village in Ba, in Viti Levu's north-west, an elder once pointed to a rock and told Reverend Marika Baleidelabaci, a Fijian historian and Methodist minister, that Jesus had been born exactly there.

title.en: Lebanon says 11 killed in Israeli airstrikes
title.zh: 黎巴嫩称以色列空袭造成11人死亡

summary.en: Lebanon's prime minister reported that 11 people were killed in Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanese villages, accusing Israel of targeting civilians in their homes. Israel stated its strikes were aimed at Hezbollah infrastructure.
summary.zh: 黎巴嫩总理报告称，以色列对黎巴嫩南部村庄的空袭造成11人死亡，并指责以色列袭击了平民住宅。以色列则表示其袭击目标是真主党的基础设施。

body.en:
Lebanon's prime minister denounced the attacks on villages in southern Lebanon for targeting civilians in their homes. Israel said it was firing on Hezbollah infrastructure.

At least 11 people were killed when Israel launched fresh airstrikes in southern Lebanon  on Saturday, the deadliest since the Israel-Hezbollah truce nearly two months ago.

The attacks were met with defiance by the Iran-backed Hezbollah , which demanded an end to "humiliating" peace negotiations with Israel .

The Lebanese Health Ministry said one of the strikes, on the edge of the village of Ansar, killed seven people and wounded two.

The strike, which happened at dawn, hit a house and destroyed it, according to NNA, the Lebanese state news agency.

Germany's DPA news agency cited residents as saying the property served as a base for Hezbollah.

The second strike hit the village of Deir al-Zahrani, killing four and wounding 17.

NNA reported other strikes around the strategic Ali Taher hill, which overlooks parts of the southern city of Nabatiyeh and key roads to it.

The Israeli military confirmed hitting Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon, saying it was retaliation for an attack by the militia on Israeli forces.

Later Saturday, Hezbollah hit back at the latest strikes, saying they would be met with an "appropriate" response.

Israel "must clearly understand that its attacks, violations and attempts to impose a fait accompli cannot continue, and will be met with an appropriate response", the Iran-backed group said in a statement.

Hezbollah warned Lebanese authorities against continuing its "humiliating" negotiations with Israel, which would provide "the enemy with free concessions."

Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam denounced the strikes, calling on Israel to "halt this escalation."

"The seven martyrs of the Israeli airstrike on the town of Ansar are not military infrastructure and the children and women killed were not military targets,” he wrote on X.

The Israel–Hezbollah war reignited in early March around the start of the  Iran war , when Hezbollah launched attacks on northern Israel to avenge the killing of Iran’s Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

It rapidly became a full-scale conflict that involved Israeli ground operations in southern Lebanon, mass evacuations of residents and the deaths of over 4,300 people.

Israel claims to have established the so-called security zone in southern Lebanon to prevent Hezbollah attacks on northern Israel. 

According to Lebanese media, the Israeli-controlled area covers approximately 620 square kilometres, or about 6% of the country's total area.

title.en: Russians snap up new homes built on Ukraine 'graveyard'
title.zh: 俄罗斯人抢购在乌克兰“墓地”上建造的新房

summary.en: Russia is constructing high-rises in the occupied Ukrainian city of Mariupol, on the sites of buildings it destroyed. Who's buying these properties? And what happened to the Ukrainians who used to lived here?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Russia is constructing high-rises in the occupied Ukrainian city of Mariupol, on the sites of buildings it destroyed. Who's buying these properties? And what happened to the Ukrainians who used to lived here?

Halyna Artemova, an English teacher, lived in Mariupol for almost 40 years, at Metallurgy Avenue 87.

"It's my beloved city. When I look at the photos, it brings tears to my eyes. I know every crack in the asphalt, every tree," she told DW. Her apartment block in the city on the Sea of Azov was struck by a missile during a Russian attack in March 2022.

Photographer Yevhen Sosnovsky and his wife lived in the house next door, Metallurgy Avenue 85, for 20 years. "I did everything myself, all the interior renovations, and the furniture," he said. "We invested a lot in it; we planned to spend our twilight years there, living quietly." His building also caught fire during the missile attack, and residents were driven out by Russian troops. They weren't even allowed to take food or clothing with them.

Now there's a parking lot where Sosnovsky's apartment block used to be. Next door, where Artemova once lived, stands a new building. The Russian building contractor Su-2007, which operates in the Ukrainian regions occupied by Russia, cleared several buildings on Metallurgy Avenue that were destroyed in the war and constructed high-rise apartment blocks in their place. These form part of a residential complex now known as the Leningradsky Kvartal.

"They're building on human bones, and fast, to eradicate the traces of their crimes," said Sosnovsky.

DW is not allowed in to the Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine, so cannot report directly from city. However, it is possible to get an idea of what life is like in Mariupol today by talking to people who used to live there, studying satellite images, and doing research online.

Many people who have moved into the new apartments on Metallurgy Avenue communicate with each other online in neighborhood forums. From these forums, it's clear that the majority bought the apartments either to live in themselves, or to rent out.

In chats, they ask how they can get furniture delivered from Russia, or which kindergarten or school they should choose for their children. People are reminded that the most important thing when submitting documents is that they should be of Russian origin.

Not everyone has finished remodeling their apartments, and some people with small children take the opportunity to complain: "It's too late! Stop the goddamn renovations! Or maybe you're pro-Ukrainian and oppose Russian laws?"

body.en:
While ongoing military actions in Gaza and settler attacks on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank have largely isolated Israel globally, Latin America's authoritarian right sees an opening for a strategic alliance.

A three-week military offensive in the Gaza Strip  in 2009, which killed more than 1,400 people, including an estimated 1,100 civilians, spurred Venezuela's Socialist president at the time, Hugo Chavez, to expel the Israeli ambassador in protest and end diplomatic relations.

Seventeen years later, Venezuela and Israel have agreed to establish a mechanism for the resumption of consular services. It's a limited step, but one that until recently would have been unthinkable.

In Colombia , the nationalist government of new President Abelardo de la Espriella recently reversed the decision by his predecessor, Gustavo Petro , to sever diplomatic relations with Israel in protest of the country's most recent war in Gaza , which has killed more than 70,000 people, nearly one-third of them children.

De la Espriella has even announced that Colombia will relocate its embassy to Jerusalem, and this week declared that Colombia would join the United States as the only two countries that recognize "Israeli sovereignty" over the Golan Heights, which is Syrian territory under international law but has been occupied by Israel since 1967. The vast majority of the international community, including Germany and the UN, does not recognize the annexation of the Golan Heights by Israel.

"There is a trend toward rapprochement with Israel as a response to the surge of the radical right in the region," said Isaac Caro, a professor at Alberto Hurtado University in Chile. Caro said authoritarians in Latin America were linking relations with Israel to "an active alignment with US foreign policy ." He said reinforcing ties with Israel had become a characteristic of Latin America's radical right as part of the renewed discourse of region's place in Judeo-Christian Western civilization.

In Argentina, for example, ultraconservative President Javier Milei has made close relations with Israel a defining feature of both his foreign policy and his own political identity.

Daniel Wajner, associate professor of international relations at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, said there had been a "surge" in diplomacy between Israel and Latin American governments. Wajner said Jair Bolsonaro , the neoliberal former president of Brazil, and El Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele, the self-described "world's coolest dictator," were early adopters of warmer ties with Israel. title.en: Donald Trump to declare Hormuz US territory 'soon'
title.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普“很快”宣布霍尔木兹为美国领土

summary.en: Donald Trump said the strait would become part of the US after Iran is defeated. He also told Americans to accept higher gas prices, which have soared since Iran closed Hormuz in response to US and Israeli attacks.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Donald Trump said the strait would become part of the US after Iran is defeated. He also told Americans to accept higher gas prices, which have soared since Iran closed Hormuz in response to US and Israeli attacks.

President Donald Trump said Friday that he would "soon" declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory.

"After we finish defeating Iran , which is being very badly defeated — pretty soon I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States," Trump said at a rally at a police academy in Garden City, New York state. "It's true," he added.

It was not clear whether his remarks were serious or whether they signal a new policy shift for Washington in its war against Tehran , which is more than five months old.

Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi dismissed Trump's remarks, saying the country would "not be intimidated" and that the strategic waterway would remain under its control and authority.

The US and Israel launched the war against Iran on February 28. At the time, senior White House officials, including Trump, said the aim was to end Iran's nuclear program and spark a popular uprising to force regime change in the Islamic Republic, among other goals.

Iran's response has been to target US allies across the Middle East with drone and missile strikes, as well as to impose a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipments passed before the war.

The US responded to Iran's closure of the strait with its own naval blockade of Iranian ships and ports. The two countries have been locked in a stalemate over the vital waterway for months, causing energy prices to soar.

Rising oil and gas costs and the economic fallout from the war are likely to be leading issues in the midterm elections in November.

During the rally, the US president also urged Americans to accept that they would have to "pay a tiny little bit more" for their gasoline as a worthy price for preventing "a very evil country" from getting a nuclear weapon.

"What we're doing is a great service for the world, not only for ourselves ... and we're really doing a ​great job," Trump told the crowd, adding that "no ships get through (the US blockade of Hormuz) unless we want them to."

On Friday, Trump also dismissed concerns over the living conditions aboard a US aircraft carrier that was deployed to the Middle East amid the war with Iran.

Relatives of service members aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln told US military media outlets that personnel are struggling with difficult living conditions and deteriorating mental health . There have also been reports of suicide attempts.

body.en: Boats carrying hundreds of people are a clear and alarming trend. But where do such large vessels come from? Providing a large dinghy for use in the choppy seas of western Europe was not a problem, as long as the order was for more than 20 vessels, they said. They had a production capacity of 500 boats a month and, yes, it was possible to get even bigger ones for the right price. They could do a seven or even an eight-metre military-style dinghy for $1,678 (£1,238) a boat, without the engines, but that would be lacking CE certification, the mandatory mark that shows a product meets EU health and safety requirements. title.en: The Fauci hearing was painful to watch. But we need answers on Covid-19’s origin| David Relman
title.zh: 福奇听证会令人痛苦，但我们需要新冠病毒起源的答案 | 大卫·雷尔曼

summary.en: Despite recent congressional hearings, understanding the origin of Covid-19 remains elusive, with a microbiologist observing a deterioration in public discourse surrounding the issue.
summary.zh: 尽管近期国会举行了听证会，但了解新冠病毒的起源仍然困难重重，一位微生物学家指出，围绕这一问题的公共讨论正在恶化。

body.en: Despite the recent hearings in Congress, we seem to be even further from the goal of understanding Covid-19’s origin’s than we have ever been As a microbiologist and infectious disease clinician, it has been tough to watch the recent devolution of public discourse on Covid-19 origins. It has been especially difficult for me to read the comments of Anthony Fauci about the origins debate in his now-public diary . And it has been painful to watch the televised spectacle hosted by the US senator Rand Paul on 29 July involving a hostile interrogation of Fauci. Despite many early pleas, including my own , for a dispassionate, objective assessment of what we know, don’t know and need to know about Covid-19 origins, we seem to be even further from this goal now than we have ever been – plagued by politicization, polarization and illogical thinking. David Relman is a professor of medicine and microbiology at Stanford University. He was an inaugural member of the US National Science Advisory Board for Biosecurity and president of the Infectious Diseases Society of America Continue reading...
body.zh: 尽管最近在国会举行了听证会，但我们似乎距离了解 Covid-19 起源的目标比以往任何时候都更远。作为一名微生物学家和传染病临床医生，很难看到最近公众关于 Covid-19 起源的讨论的转移。对我来说，阅读安东尼·福奇在他现已公开的日记中关于起源争论的评论尤其困难。 7 月 29 日美国参议员兰德·保罗主持的电视节目对福奇进行敌意审讯，令人感到痛苦。尽管包括我自己在内的许多人早期呼吁对我们所知道、不知道和需要了解的 Covid-19 起源进行冷静、客观的评估，但我们现在似乎比以往任何时候都离这个目标更远——受到政治化、两极分化和不合逻辑思维的困扰。大卫·雷尔曼是斯坦福大学医学和微生物学教授。他是美国国家生物安全科学咨询委员会的首任成员和美国传染病学会主席继续阅读...

Proverbs 18:17 suggests that true understanding emerges only after hearing all sides and carefully scrutinizing every claim. This calls for patience and a commitment to truth beyond...

summary.en: Taiwan conducted its first internet blackout simulation, prompted by concerns over the security of its undersea cables, which are vital for its digital connectivity. During the exercise in Taipei, air raid sirens sounded, mobile alerts pinged, and police directed people off the streets.
summary.zh: 台湾周四首次进行互联网中断模拟演习，原因是担心作为其“数字生命线”的海底电缆的安全。在台北的演习中，防空警报响起，手机警报提示音不断，警察引导人们离开街道。

body.en: Taiwan practised cutting off internet for the first time amid concerns about the safety of the undersea cables that form its ‘digital lifeline’ In Taipei, the streets swiftly empty as air raid sirens ring out and alerts ping on mobile phones. Police officers usher any stragglers into shelters, leaving the capital suddenly deserted. In cities across Taiwan, these kinds of drills are a fact of life every year , amid the growing threat posed by China across the strait, but this time there is something different. Continue reading...

This spiritual anchor can guide communities as...

verse.textEn: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God.
verse.textZh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在；不要惊惶，因为我是你的神。

title.en: The west turns a blind eye to Xi Jinping’s repressive regime in China | Letters
title.zh: 西方国家对习近平在中国的压制性政权视而不见 | 来信

summary.en: Jennifer Hubbard and other letter writers express concern that Western nations are ignoring China's repressive regime, particularly its 'ethnic unity' law used to suppress minorities. They argue that meaningful international diplomacy is urgently needed to address these human rights issues.
summary.zh: 詹妮弗·哈伯德及其他来信者表示，西方国家对中国压制性政权，特别是其用于压制少数民族的“民族团结”法视而不见。他们认为，急需有意义的国际外交来解决这些人权问题。

body.en: Meaningful diplomacy on an international level is well overdue, writes Jennifer Hubbard . Plus letters from Geoffrey Dixon and Jane Renton In his article on China’s latest tool for suppression of minorities, the “ethnic unity” law, Simon Tisdall seems to take it as read that western governments will continue to pay lip service to notions of human rights in China while pursuing short-term economic goals, ultimately destructive to their own productivity ( President Xi never wastes a good crisis. As Iran, Ukraine and Palestine distract the world, he tightens his grip, 8 August ). This has been the pattern since June 1989, the Tiananmen Square massacre. His faint hope that the young urban Chinese might overturn Xi’s regime is a judgment on the failure of western governments to show any foresight, integrity, effective diplomacy, joined-up thinking or action. They rely on the self-sacrifice of individuals such as Jimmy Lai , Lobga Rangzen and countless – often to us nameless – individuals who put their lives on the line while we wring our hands and weep crocodile tears. Continue reading...
body.zh: 詹妮弗·哈伯德写道，早就应该在国际层面开展有意义的外交。再加上杰弗里·迪克森和简·伦顿的来信。西蒙·蒂斯达尔在其关于中国镇压少数民族的最新工具“民族团结”法的文章中似乎认为，西方政府将继续对中国的人权观念口头上说好，同时追求短期经济目标，最终损害他们自己的生产力（习主席从来不会浪费一场好的危机。随着伊朗、乌克兰和巴勒斯坦分散了世界的注意力，他加强了控制，8月8日）。这就是1989年6月天安门广场屠杀以来的模式。他对中国城市年轻人可能推翻习近平政权的微弱希望是对西方政府未能表现出任何远见、正直、有效外交、联合思维或行动的判断。他们依赖于黎智英（Jimmy Lai）、洛布加·让赞（Lobga Rangzen）等个人的自我牺牲，以及无数（通常对我们来说无名）个人的自我牺牲，他们冒着生命危险，而我们则绞尽脑汁，流下鳄鱼的眼泪。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The call for international diplomacy to address the suppression of minorities echoes the biblical mandate to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves. In a world where powerful voices can overshadow the vulnerable, Yahweh reminds us of our responsibility to advocate for justice and the rights of the destitute. May we seek wisdom and courage to uphold...
reflection.zh: 呼吁国际外交以解决少数民族受压迫的问题，与圣经中为不能为自己说话之人发声的命令不谋而合。在一个强大声音可能掩盖弱势群体的世界里，雅伟提醒我们有责任倡导正义和维护贫困者的权利。愿我们寻求智慧和勇气，维护所有人的尊严，特别是那些声音被压制的人。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.

title.en: Taiwan says it was hit by ‘abnormal’ AI-assisted cyber-attack
title.zh: 台湾称遭受“异常”人工智能辅助网络攻击

summary.en: Taiwan reported detecting "abnormal" AI-assisted cyber-attacks on government agencies last month, originating from overseas. These attacks represent a new kind of threat, with suspected links to China-based hackers.
summary.zh: 台湾报告称，上个月侦测到来自海外、由人工智能辅助的“异常”网络攻击，目标是政府机构。这些攻击代表了一种新型威胁，据称与中国相关黑客有关。

body.en: Taiwan’s statement comes a day after reports that suspected China-linked hackers had carried out a first-of-a-kind breach Taiwan says it detected AI-assisted cyber-attacks on government agencies that came from overseas last month, a new kind of threat that has been reported as “first-of-a-kind breach”. The Ministry of Digital Affairs (MDA) said its cybersecurity monitoring units ‌detected the “abnormal attack” targeting government agencies, which began on 20 July. The National Institute of Cyber Security issued a series of warning alerts while it investigated. Continue reading...

reflection.en: The emergence of AI-assisted cyber-attacks highlights the constant need for vigilance in a rapidly changing world. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us that wisdom lies in foreseeing danger and taking appropriate refuge. As technology evolves, so must our discernment and protective measures, trusting Yahweh for guidance.
reflection.zh: 人工智能辅助的网络攻击的出现，凸显了在快速变化的世界中保持警惕的持续必要性。箴言27:12提醒我们，智慧在于预见危险并采取适当的避难措施。随着科技发展，我们的洞察力和保护措施也必须随之进步，信靠雅伟的指引。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.

title.en: With Hollywood struggling in China, can the Odyssey draw a crowd?
title.zh: 好莱坞在中国市场举步维艰，《奥德赛》能否吸引观众？

summary.en: Christopher Nolan's summer blockbuster, "The Odyssey" (likely Oppenheimer), is set for release across China's Imax screens. This comes at a time when Western films generally face difficulties in the Chinese market, and the film itself has reportedly overcome significant opposition.
summary.zh: 克里斯托弗·诺兰的夏季大片《奥德赛》（很可能是《奥本海默》）将在中国各地的IMAX影院上映。目前西方电影在中国市场普遍举步维艰，而这部影片据报道也克服了来自世界首富的猛烈攻击。

title.en: Government admits NDIS reforms will impact families, downplays fears over state readiness

summary.en: The federal disability minister has defended changes to the NDIS, flagging further amendments to tackle fraud and win parliamentary support.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Labor has downplayed concerns that state-based disability supports won't be ready when needed, as the government pushes contentious NDIS reforms targeting fraud and spending through parliament.

A government-led Senate inquiry on Friday recommended National Disability Insurance Scheme changes should be passed with no substantial alterations.

The overhaul would cut a targeted $37.8 billion from the NDIS over four years and remove 160,000 participants by tightening eligibility requirements.

NDIS Minister Jenny McAllister said a deal between the government and the coalition to pass the changes was getting close.

"We're really hopeful and I'd go as far as saying confident that we can reach an agreement," she told ABC's Insiders program on Sunday.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Opposition health spokeswoman Anne Ruston called for a strengthened fraud and corruption response within the disability insurance agency in the inquiry report.

Senator McAllister said the government was still considering evidence brought forward during the inquiry process and flagged fraud as an area to work through with the coalition.

But concerns about the changes remain among advocates — and from at least one state.

In a joint statement, 12 disability advocacy organisations said the reforms should not pass parliament in their current form.

"It must guarantee that people are not diverted from, or lose, NDIS supports unless alternative supports are funded, operational, accessible and available in practice."

Queensland has resisted signing up to the Thriving Kids program, a major plank in federal plans to cut costs from the NDIS.

Under the program, which is due to be rolled out from October, some children aged eight and under with autism or developmental delays would be shifted onto state supports.

Queensland Disability Minister Amanda Camm has refused to back the agreement, labelling the change a cost-shifting exercise that lacked detail.

Despite the conflict, Labor remained confident people with a disability would not be left without the support they needed.

"We don't need to contemplate delay at this point, because we are working with the states and territories toward that January 1 deadline."

Labor's NDIS plan would lead to average funding being cut by about $5000 a year for participants.

"It is a reduction and we don't deny that it will have impacts on people with disability and their families," Senator McAllister said.

She again dismissed calls to introduce an NDIS inspector-general, saying it would risk adding another layer of bureaucracy.

Pauline Hanson has doubled down on notorious decades-old comments criticising Sydney's Mardi Gras, saying she thinks people should keep their sexuality "behind closed doors".

The comments come only days after a colleague declared One Nation "one of the gayest parties in Australia".

In an infamous 1996 interview with 60 Minutes, the right-wing party's leader responded "I don't like it" while offering her thoughts on the annual LGBTIQ+ festival.

"I don't like it because it's promoting something ... that is not natural," she said at the time.

Her "I don't like it" comment was co-opted by drag queen Pauline Pantsdown in 1998 and remixed into a parody dance song, which made it into the Triple J Hottest 100 list of that year.

Three decades later, Senator Hanson said she acknowledged the economic benefit of the pride parade, adding that it was "acceptable" Australia had legalised gay marriage.

"I still don't like the gay Mardi Gras, but that's my opinion," she told News24 on Sunday.

"I think your own, personal sexuality should be kept ... behind closed doors. It's no one's business to do it out there with the gay Mardi Gras anywhere.

"I know it brings a lot of tourists to the country. I know it brings a lot of money. I know all this, but that’s my personal opinion. But anyway, good luck to them that they want to do that."

Her comments follow revelations One Nation's candidate for Western Australia's upper house at the 2025 election, Parminder Singh, made several anti-gay comments in a video on social media.

Mr Singh, who was third on One Nation's upper house ticket at the state election, has since been removed from the party's website, after the video became public.

During the week, One Nation MP Barnaby distanced the party from its former candidate's views, describing it as "one of the gayest parties in Australia".

Senator Hanson also rejected Ms Singh's comments, saying she never heard similar views from him when he was a candidate.

The firebrand politician also defended her inability to name the leaders of crucial allies and regional powers when questioned about her foreign policy credentials as a would-be prime minister.

In an earlier interview with News24, the One Nation leader said diplomacy with Australia's neighbours would pose "no problem", despite her notoriously using her maiden speech in 1996 to declare the nation was "in danger of being swamped by Asians".

Asked if she could name the president of Indonesia or the prime minister of Japan, two major regional powers and key Australian trading partners, Senator Hanson said she couldn't.

body.en:
An agreement has been struck on a major federal-state gun buyback following the Bondi shooting massacre, with the Commonwealth and New South Wales governments to evenly share the cost of the scheme.

NSW tightened its laws in the days following the December 2025 attack by introducing gun ownership limits, reclassifying some types of weapons, boosting background checks and reducing firearms licences from five years to two.

The buyback is now considered the next step in the reforms — and is informed by the interim recommendations of the anti-Semitism royal commission.

"We must do everything we can to make sure the anti-Semitic terrorist attack in Bondi doesn't happen again," Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Sunday.

But the hope for a truly national scheme is far from certain. NSW is so far the only state to come aboard, with several states rejecting joining outright — and it also faces mounting opposition from political parties, including One Nation.

The first phase of the scheme, set to begin on 2 November 2026, will see $1,000 paid to people who hand in their revolvers, $850 for semi-automatic handguns, $850 for double-barrel shotguns and $650 for those with a single barrel.

Compensation will be paid for firearms beyond the new ownership limits and for newly reclassified firearms, along with a flat fee for associated ammunition.

The scheme will also provide financial assistance for businesses and industry to adjust to the reforms.

The Commonwealth will contribute 50 per cent for administration costs and fully fund the destruction of surrendered weapons. 

A fixed price schedule will apply for individual licence holders beyond the new legal limit to return their firearms in exchange for compensation.

Eligible businesses and dealers will be offered up to $25,000 in grants and one-off licence fee relief worth $500 over two years per dealer.

Early 2027 will see a pathway to compensation, for a fee, for eligible higher-value firearms with an indicative market value above $3,000 and capped at $10,000 per firearm.

It's estimated up to 274,000 registered firearms or about 24 per cent of the total number of registered guns in NSW — and some 50,000 licence holders — are affected by the new limits on ownership. 

The buyback scheme has been branded a national one — though NSW is the only state participating right now.

Queensland and Victoria have rejected the scheme outright, while the NT was firm that it would not fund a buyback.

title.en: Property investors are retreating — so why isn't this a win for first-home buyers?

summary.en: New data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics indicates an 8.6 per cent drop in investor loans during the June quarter, raising questions about the long-term presence of investors in the housing market.

body.en:
Investors are shying away from the housing market — but experts say it might not be the win the government says it is.

New Australian Bureau of Statistics data on loans show investors have pulled back sharply from the housing market in the June quarter.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers said on Friday the lending figures were an "encouraging sign" that Labor's changes to negative gearing and the capital gains discount were working as intended and the market was "shifting in favour of first-home buyers" — even before the changes have officially taken effect.

But experts said the retreat hasn't necessarily translated into the wave of first-home buyers the federal government's property tax changes were designed to generate.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The number of investor loans fell 8.6 per cent in the June quarter, while first-home buyer loans fell a comparatively lower 2.9 per cent, according to ABS data released on Friday.

Independent property researcher Cameron Kusher said ABS' latest lending data was not surprising and reflected a typical knee-jerk reaction to policy changes.

“Across both the number and the value, the biggest falls in lending over the quarter were for investors, which is not really a surprise when you consider the tax changes that have happened,” he said.

The pullback lines up with what major banks have been reporting in their own lending figures, with CBA and NAB both reporting a 15 per cent drop in mortgage applications last quarter, while Westpac saw a 20 per cent drop.

The tax changes were announced in the May budget but aren't set to formally take effect until 1 July 2027. So, this quarter's fall was a reaction to the announcement itself, not the policy in action.

"We may actually see a larger fall when we get to the next quarter, when we see the full impact of a whole quarter of these changes," he said.

Both Kusher and Real Estate Group's economist Luc Redman say investors have not retreated entirely, rather they have changed strategy.

They are still keen on residential property but the type of property they’re chasing has shifted. They are now eyeing properties that have strong rental growth, or yield.

"Early evidence post-budget suggests that investors are enquiring more towards units that tend to have a higher yield and a lower entry point … compared to prior, when investors would be looking at houses that have stronger prospects of capital growth," Redman told SBS News.

title.en: 'Broken and grateful': Alice Springs farewells Kumanjayi Little Baby
title.zh: “心碎又感激”：爱丽斯泉告别库曼贾伊小宝贝

summary.en: There was a sombre atmosphere at Kumanjayi Little Baby's funeral, with speeches punctuated by the cries of mourners.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
WARNING: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this story includes the name and image of an Indigenous person who has passed away.

Alice Springs is known as the Red Centre of Australia but on 15 August, the community donned pink for the funeral of five-year-old Warlpiri girl, Kumanjayi Little Baby .

Warlpiri Elder and family spokesperson Robin Granites said pink was her favourite colour — it "reminds us of the clothes she used to wear".

"And the times when we would go in the evening, you see the sunset and even the early morning, you see the pink colour of clouds and that ... is a really good colour for us," Granites said ahead of the funeral.

Kumanjayi Little Baby's body was found on 30 April, after she went missing from Old Timers town camp, south of Alice Springs. Her disappearance sparked a five-day search, described as one of the largest search efforts in Northern Territory history.

47-year-old Jefferson Lewis has since been charged with her alleged murder and two other offences that cannot be published for legal reasons .

Pastor Rejeili Paulo-Smith spoke on behalf of Kumanjayi Little Baby's mother at the funeral service.

She requested that her daughter be remembered , "for who she was, not simply for the tragedy of how her life ended".

"Kumanjayi wasn't simply a little girl who was known by the community. She was Mum's baby too. She was a little girl whose presence filled their home and whose absence has left an enormous space," Paulo-Smith said.

It's been almost four months since the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby. During this time, her family and Indigenous communities have engaged in the grieving period and mourning process known as Sorry Business .

In recent months, Paulo-Smith said the community had felt "both broken and grateful".

"Broken because a precious little life has been taken from us far too soon, yet grateful because Kumanjayi Little Baby was here. She was known, she was loved, she mattered," she said.

The week following Kumanjayi Little Baby's death, thousands of Australians gathered at nationwide candlelight vigils.

At a local vigil in Alice Springs, 89-year-old Maya Cifali told NITV News the outpouring of community spirit was unlike anything she had ever seen.

"It is the first time that such a community spirit is felt for all of us," Cifali said.

Granites also believes the local community has displayed the Warlpiri concept of Jintangka; "which means we're all in one, everyone together".

At the funeral, he took the opportunity to thank Australians and people overseas for rallying behind his family during and in the months following the search...

title.en: Beautiful, remote and running on diesel: The Daintree's power struggle
title.zh: 居住在澳洲天堂的隐性成本

summary.en: They left the city for a paradise. Now Daintree residents are asking how long they can afford to stay.
summary.zh: 他们离开了城市，去往一个天堂般的地方。现在，丹特里居民们正在思考他们还能在那里住多久。

body.en:

In her backyard, Tamara Scenna takes a deep breath beneath the towering canopy of the Daintree Rainforest in Far North Queensland.

Streams of light filter through layers of ferns and fan palms as she pauses beside a running stream.

Birds sing in an off-beat chorus, providing a tranquil soundtrack to one of the oldest rainforests.

It's the perfect setting for forest bathing — a Japanese practice of immersing oneself in nature.

"I think it's about seeing the forest differently and being able to almost be given permission to slow down and stop and just be," Scenna tells SBS News.

"It took a while to slow down and really have a city adrenaline stop, but after a couple of months we sort of went, 'actually we don't want to go to the city anymore'.

But behind the tranquillity lies a challenge shared by many of the Daintree's roughly 700 residents. Living beyond the electricity grid means finding ways to balance life in this remote rainforest with the realities of modern living.

In 2021, Scenna and her family swapped life in Sydney for the quiet of the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Daintree Rainforest.

Hoping to escape the pace of city life, her family spent a year travelling around Australia before deciding they were ready for a change.

The journey led the couple to settle in the rainforest, with Scenna leaving her public sector job to run a caravan park and restaurant with her husband , Bruno.

But the dream of living among the ancient trees comes with practical challenges. Like many residents in the region, the couple must find their own solutions for powering their home and business.

While the Scennas have a hybrid energy system that includes solar, relying on diesel generators remains a necessity.

They paid about $300,000 for the solar that powers around a third of their business.

Bruno says installing enough solar panels to power their entire operation would be expensive and require clearing more rainforest for additional infrastructure.

"From an environmental perspective, why would you do that when you can have renewable energy? I fundamentally don't understand," he tells SBS News.

Growing uncertainty around fuel costs, including volatility linked to global events , has renewed calls from residents for a renewable energy solution in the Daintree.

In 2022, a solar-based microgrid project received a funding commitment of $18.75 million from the then Coalition federal government, with funding to start in 2025.

reflection.en: Many seek an earthly paradise, investing their hopes and resources into a beautiful place or ideal lifestyle. This story reminds us that even the most idyllic earthly treasures can come with hidden costs, making them unsustainable or fleeting. It prompts us to consider where our true and lasting treasures lie.
